answer: Stop sybils with a kernel tide harbor: an agent bonds one harbor. Each cycle it sets one kernel afloat on its tide; verifiers match the kernel's waterline height to the harbor chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 harbors at 18x: one kernel floats once in one harbor, its height set by that tide alone, unrepeatable elsewhere, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents float once, keep rights.
